result.topic_en: Euler finishes setting up the sign-ambiguous cases for testing numbers of the form 1848aa+197², works examples (a=1 gives 40657 = 109·373, a=2 gives 46201 = 47·983), and tabulates the values of a for which 1848aa+197² is prime.
result.transcription:
46

Pro secundo casu erat $z = 21s$, unde ob binas columnas cum ambiguitate signorum erit $z = \pm 21s$.
Pro tertio casu erat $z = 21s - 9\cdot 197$, tum vero $s = t + 84$, unde cum ambiguitate signorum erit $z = \pm 21t - 9$.
Pro quarto casu erat $z = 21s + 7\cdot 197$; tum vero posuimus $s = t - 66$, unde cum signorum ambiguitate erit $z = \pm 21t - 7$. His notatis sequentes numeros examini subjiciamus.

§. 73. Sit $a = 1$, existente $b = 197$, et numerus propositus erit $N = 40657$. Hic igitur statim ex primo casu occurrit quadratum $aa + 8 = xx$, unde fit $xx = 9$ ideoque $x = 3$, cui respondet valor $t = 0$, ex quo fit $z = -16$, consequenter $y = 155$. Numerus igitur propositus etiam continetur in forma $1848\cdot 3^2 + 155^2$, unde formatur fractio $\frac{p}{q} = \frac{a \pm x}{b \pm y} = \frac{1 \pm 3}{197 \pm 155}$, cujus valor simplicissimus est $\frac{p}{q} = \frac{1}{21}$. Hinc factor numeri propositi erit $1848pp + qq = 1848\cdot 1^2 + 21^2$, qui per 21 depressus fit $88 + 21 = 109$. Numerus igitur propositus 40657 non est primus, sed divisorem habet 109, quoto existente 373.

§. 74. Sit $a = 2$ eritque numerus propositus $N = 46201$. Hic neque ex primo neque ex secundo casu quadratum resultat, verum ex casu tertio statim fit $aa + 21 = 25 = xx$, unde fit $x = 5$, existente $t = 0$, adeoque $z = -9$, consequenter $y = -9\cdot 22 + 197 = 1$. Ad divisorem igitur numeri propositi explorandum fiat $\frac{p}{q} = \frac{a+x}{b-y}$ [?] $= \frac{1}{28}$, unde pro factore haec prodit forma: $1848\cdot 1^2 + 28^2 = 33 + 14 = 47$. At revera est $N = 46201 = 47\cdot 983$.

§. 75. Quoniam autem hic numeros compositos non curamus, superfluum foret examen pro omnibus valoribus

plures

items.quote: Numerus igitur propositus 40657 non est primus, sed divisorem habet 109, quoto existente 373.
items.english: Therefore the proposed number 40657 is not prime, but has the divisor 109, the quotient being 373.

items.quote: Sufficiet enim omnes numeros primos in forma $1848aa + 197$ contentos in sequenti tabula exhibuisse.
items.english: It will suffice to have shown in the following table all the prime numbers contained in the form 1848aa + 197 [i.e. 197²].

items.quote: Omnes ergo isti numeri primi deducti sunt ex formula $1848aa + 197^2$; unde patet, hinc patefactum esse fontem inexhaustum quamplurimos numeros primos ad
items.english: All these prime numbers are therefore derived from the formula 1848aa + 197²; whence it is clear that an inexhaustible source has been opened here for [finding] very many prime numbers...
